thesis: Dell's Q2 FY27 report (Sept 1) showed a confirmed beat-and-raise: record $60.9B AI server orders, a record $95B backlog, and guidance raised to ~$192B revenue / $25.50 non-GAAP EPS, pushing shares to a fresh 52-week high. The main bear argument -- that AI-server mix carries structurally lower gross margins -- doesn't change the near-term read, since management's own raised guidance already reflects that mix shift and the record backlog gives multi-quarter revenue visibility that should support continued operating leverage even as blended margins normalize lower.
invalidation: A pullback in disclosed AI-server backlog/bookings in a future quarter, or gross margin compression beyond what current guidance already implies, would undercut this thesis.

thesis: Nvidia's Q2 FY27 report (Aug 26) beat on record $89B data-center revenue and guided Q3 to $108B, and the company followed with two confirmed, disclosed deals -- a ~$12.9B Hugging Face acquisition and a $3.5B MediaTek investment -- extending the stock to within 3% of its 52-week high. The 'AI bubble' capex-sustainability concern doesn't change the near-term read: Nvidia's own guidance conservatively assumes zero China data-center compute revenue, so the disclosed backlog and guide already reflect contracted, not speculative, demand.
invalidation: A miss or guide-down in a future quarter, or a confirmed pullback in hyperscaler capex commitments, would undercut this thesis.

thesis: AMD's Q2 report (Aug 4) beat on revenue and EPS with accelerating growth (Q3 guided +41% YoY), but a gross-margin miss (54% vs 56% consensus) triggered a 'sell the news' reaction, and subsequent analyst downgrades cite rising hyperscaler custom-silicon competition (Broadcom, Google TPU, AWS Trainium) as a threat to AMD's AI-GPU share. Consensus price targets still imply significant upside from here, but this bull/bear debate over margin trajectory and competitive positioning remains genuinely unresolved rather than settled by either side.
invalidation: A further gross-margin miss, or confirmed hyperscaler design wins shifting decisively to competitors' custom silicon, would weaken this thesis; a margin recovery or new large customer disclosure would strengthen it.

thesis: Marvell's Q2 FY27 report (Aug 27) beat and raised guidance on record data-center revenue, including a newly disclosed Google custom-silicon agreement, but the stock fell on gross-margin compression (mix shift to lower-margin ASIC work) and FY28 data-center growth guidance seen as trailing peers like Broadcom. The bull case -- that margin dilution is an acceptable tradeoff for ASIC-driven growth -- hasn't been resolved by the market, which kept selling into early September despite the raised guidance.
invalidation: A further gross-margin guide-down, or evidence the Google/ASIC pipeline is slowing, would weaken this thesis; margin stabilization or new hyperscaler design wins would strengthen it.

thesis: Vertiv's Q2 2026 report (Jul 29) missed on revenue (management attributed it to project-timing shifts, not demand) while beating on EPS and raising full-year guidance across all metrics; orders grew 46% YoY against 24% revenue growth, pointing to a near-record backlog. Shares fell ~17% that day and have continued drifting lower into September despite the guidance raise, so the market has not yet fully accepted management's 'timing, not demand' framing.
invalidation: A further revenue miss next quarter, or evidence the order/backlog growth is decelerating, would undercut this thesis; a bounce-back quarter matching the raised guidance would confirm it.

thesis: AXT's 60-day pullback followed a strong Q2 (record $47.6M revenue +164% YoY, return to profitability, >$100M backlog, raised Q3 guidance) and a subsequent spike into the $80s-$90s; the decline since reflects profit-taking/valuation-reset off that spike rather than any new negative disclosure, per available reporting. Analyst consensus remains Buy with price targets well above the current price, but the move itself is characterized as technical/sentiment-driven rather than a fundamental deterioration.
invalidation: A confirmed slowdown in indium-phosphide/GaAs substrate demand, a China export-license disruption, or a guidance cut would undercut this thesis.

thesis: Intel's ~25% 60-day decline followed a Q2 beat, but the drop is explained by three confirmed, disclosed factors layered together: a dilutive $20B common stock offering (closed Aug 12), continued ~$2.1B quarterly Foundry operating losses, and x86 CPU/server market share falling to a 30-year low against AMD. Government and strategic-investor backing (US, Nvidia, SoftBank) and improving 18A yields are real counterpoints, but they don't offset the direct EPS dilution already taken or the structural share-loss trend, which remain unresolved.
invalidation: A Foundry return to breakeven, confirmed large external customer design wins on 18A, or a reversal in x86 share losses would undercut this avoid call.

thesis: Samsara's Q2 FY27 report (Sept 3) beat and raised full-year guidance, but shares reversed from an initial ~14% premarket pop to close down roughly 10%, a 'sell the news' reaction against a stretched valuation (P/S ~12x); a recent analyst downgrade also cited decelerating app-download trends as an early signal of slowing growth. The beat-and-raise fundamentals and the market's same-day rejection of them point in opposite directions, an unresolved read rather than a clear signal.
invalidation: Confirmed reacceleration in usage/app-engagement trends, or the stock stabilizing above the pre-earnings level, would undercut this avoid call.

thesis: Sunbelt Rentals' volume spike appears to be sentiment/positioning-driven -- continued selling after a Sept 1 JPMorgan downgrade (Underweight, margin concerns following a prior-quarter EBITDA-margin miss) heading into Q1 FY27 earnings due Sept 9, rather than any single confirmed catalyst dated to today. With that earnings print just days away and margin guidance already under analyst scrutiny, this reads as a technical/pre-event drift rather than a resolved fundamental signal.
invalidation: A Q1 FY27 print (Sept 9) that stabilizes or beats margin expectations would undercut this avoid call; a further margin miss would confirm it.
